# HAND-BUILT FIXTURE — written from the output format `checkupdates`
# (pacman-contrib) and `pacman -Qu` share: `<name> <installed> ->
# <available>`, one package per line. It is not a transcript of a real
# system's output; the package versions were written by hand to be plausible.
#
# Still owed: a real run on an Arch system that also carries AUR packages,
# recorded with `LC_ALL=C checkupdates > fixture.txt`.
#
# What this fixture proves about an AUR-carrying host is a negative, and it is
# the honest one. Both commands answer from the sync databases, so packages
# built from the AUR — on such a host these are typically things like `yay`,
# `obsidian-native` or a `-bin` AUR build — do not appear in this output at
# all: there is no sync database entry for them to be out of date against. A
# row for an AUR package could only be written by inventing an available
# version no repository ever announced, so none is produced, and the operator
# who wants those updates is served by an AUR helper, not by this scan.
#
# The lines that are not `name installed -> available` are the noise pacman
# writes to the same stream a deployment captures, in the C locale: the message
# for an IgnorePkg entry, and the one `checkupdates` emits when the file
# database was never downloaded. The parser skips them — treating either as a
# package row would name a version nobody offered.
warning: package files is not installed (or is corrupted): run 'pacman -Fy' to download it
pacman 7.1.0-2 -> 7.2.0-1
lib32-nvidia-utils 580.95.05-1 -> 580.105.08-1
warning: gcc: ignoring package upgrade (15.2.1+r26-1 => 16.1.1-2)
